children: Johnson Controls reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 sales of $7.1 billion, up 10%, with organic sales growth of 12%. GAAP diluted EPS was $1.60 and adjusted diluted EPS was $1.66. The company also reported strong orders and backlog and initiated fiscal 2027 guidance.
Q4 net sales were $7.113 billion, compared with $6.442 billion a year earlier; organic sales increased 12%.
Gross profit was $2.705 billion, versus $2.351 billion in Q4 FY25.
Q4 EBIT was $1.145 billion; adjusted EBIT was $1.299 billion.
Net income attributable to Johnson Controls from continuing operations was $967 million. GAAP diluted EPS was $1.60, and adjusted diluted EPS was $1.66.
For FY27, the company forecast organic sales growth of 11% to 12%, operating leverage of at least 30%, adjusted EPS of $6.15 to $6.30, and adjusted free cash flow conversion of approximately 95%.
Orders increased 44% organically year over year, and backlog reached $23.0 billion, up 43% organically.
Americas demand was supported by data centers, Applied HVAC and Controls; regional orders rose 58% and backlog increased 54% year over year.
EMEA organic sales grew 3%; the company cited continued pressure from conflicts in the Middle East.
APAC organic sales increased 13%, led by 15% growth in Products and Systems and continued strength in Applied HVAC.
Across the regions, the company cited productivity improvements and favorable business mix as contributors to segment performance.
